uminho-azurem.name: University of Minho – Azurém Campus
uminho-azurem.short: The University of Minho's engineering campus in Guimarães, with its schools of engineering, architecture and design by the old town
uminho-azurem.long: The Azurém Campus is the University of Minho's site in Guimarães, a few minutes from the historic centre. The university was founded in 1973 and began teaching in 1975/76. The campus is home to the School of Engineering, the School of Architecture, Art and Design, and part of the School of Sciences. Its organising axis was laid out by the architect Bartolomeu Costa Cabral in the 1980s; the architecture school building (no. 09) was designed by Fernando Távora and José Bernardo Távora and opened in 2004. The campus library specialises in engineering, architecture, geography and planning, and from the campus you can see Guimarães Castle.
uminho-azurem.history:
The University of Minho is a public university founded in 1973 and teaching since the 1975/76 academic year. It belongs to the group of "new universities" that reshaped Portuguese higher education. By 2025 it had about 21,000 students. Its premises are split between Braga and Guimarães; the Azurém Campus is the main one in Guimarães.

The campus stands beside the historic centre, which is unusual for a modern university. Azurém houses the School of Engineering, where almost all of its courses are taught, the School of Architecture, Art and Design (EAAD), and some courses of the School of Sciences and the Institute of Social Sciences. The School of Engineering celebrates its anniversary on 7 October in the campus's main auditorium.

The campus was built up over several decades. Its first organising axis was traced by the architect Bartolomeu Costa Cabral in the 1980s. Building 09, which houses the School of Architecture, Art and Design, was designed by the architects Fernando Távora and José Bernardo Távora and opened in 2004. It extends the campus's original axis and faces the new buildings of the School of Sciences, designed by Atelier 15. The teaching blocks are mostly long, light slabs set among greenery, separated by footpaths and gardens.

The university library in Guimarães (BPG) is also on the Azurém Campus. Its collection covers every branch of engineering, the history of populations, geography and planning, and is arranged by the Universal Decimal Classification. In recent years a new library has also opened on the campus. Besides teaching buildings, the site has research centres, student residences and sports facilities, and covers about 18 hectares.

The Azurém Campus is not a tourist sight but a working part of the city. Its open layout, modern buildings and the view of Guimarães Castle nonetheless make it a notable point on the city map, especially for anyone interested in the modern Portuguese architecture of the Távora school.

uminho-azurem.tip: The campus is open to walkers; the main entrance is on the south-west, off Alameda da Universidade. Teaching buildings can be entered during class hours, and the library is open to readers. From the historic centre it is about a 20-minute walk or a couple of stops on a city bus. While you are there, look at Guimarães Castle from the campus — it gives an unusual angle on it.
